milestone: A small patient group starts contributing natural history data a future trial could use, and chooses its first research partner.

retrospective.title: What sharing a mechanism has already done once
retrospective.summary: STXBP1 families waited about 13 years from the gene's discovery to the first gene-specific trial. SLC6A1 families entered a trial about 6 years after their gene's discovery, by joining the STXBP1 trial on a shared protein-misfolding rationale. VAMP2 families are 7.5 years in with no trial, and VAMP2 shares the fusion machinery with STXBP1.
retrospective.caveat: One comparison is not proof that sharing caused the faster route; other factors (the drug was already approved, the same investigators) also mattered.

existing_route.step: Find out who else works on this biology
existing_route.how: Conferences, cold emails and reading the literature one gene at a time.
existing_route.basis: SLC6A1 families reached a shared trial 6 years after their gene was discovered; VAMP2 families are 7.5 years in without one.

existing_route.step: Build your own registry or natural history study
existing_route.how: Apply to a registry programme, recruit families, collect data.
existing_route.time: Five years or more of data collection
existing_route.basis: NORD's registry programme asks new natural history studies to run for at least five years.

atlas_route.step: See your mechanism neighbours, existing assets and partners
atlas_route.how: One search: diseases that share the mechanism, assets that already accept your disease, people already working across your genes. Every link sourced.

atlas_route.step: Expert review of what must be checked
atlas_route.how: The atlas lists the biological and eligibility questions an expert should answer before two communities join forces.

atlas_route.step: Join what exists instead of rebuilding it
atlas_route.how: Enrol in the multi-gene registry that already lists your gene, and propose your disease as an arm of an existing natural history study or outcome-measure effort.

assumptions: The existing asset accepts the new disease. True today for Simons Searchlight and VAMP2; it still has to be confirmed for the STXBP1 natural history study and outcome-measure consortium.
The mechanism overlap is close enough for shared outcome measures or a shared trial design. The atlas flags this as an expert question; it is not assumed.
Consent and data-sharing terms allow families of a new disease to join.
The atlas covers the relevant biology. Today it maps one mechanism family in depth.
validate_next: Walk a real patient group (for example VAMP2's) through the journey and time each step against their actual history.
Have rare-disease advisors score the atlas's first-draft landscape against their own assessments.
Track how many atlas links survive expert review, alongside the agreement between two independent extractions.

sources_checked.note: New registries commit to running a natural history study for at least five years.
